$comment: The third-party plugin roster. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for what the
install engine installs into the web profile. It replaces the hard-coded
`pnpm_ins` calls in step_install_plugins() of dotfiles-ai/sync.sh, and the
hand-maintained `expected` array in step_report_extra_plugins() is derived from
it rather than kept in sync by hand.
Format: JSON, not YAML. Same reason as config/migration-map.json: Thursday must
be validatable on a bare checkout with plain `node`, which parses JSON natively
and has no YAML parser. Consistency with the migration map matters more than
preference. The one thing YAML would have bought -- comments -- is carried by
the mandatory `why` field on every entry, by `notes`, and by `hazards`.
THE COMMENTS IN sync.sh ARE THE VALUABLE PART. They record failures that were
already paid for once: duplicate loader entry ids, double-registered tools,
an npm release that ships fewer tools than the bundled one, four upstream
compaction bugs. Every one of them is carried here as a field value. When you
bump a pin, you are responsible for re-reading that entry's `hazards` first.
This file does not install anything and does not encode install ORDER: sync.sh
collects every spec and hands them to one `dsh plugin add`, whose reconcile step
mounts them all. Order in this array is grouping, not sequence.

fieldSyntax.id: stable slug for this entry; referenced by tickets and by the composition patch
fieldSyntax.packageName: the name the package is installed UNDER, i.e. the key that appears in the web profile's dependencies. For an aliased install this is NOT the upstream package name; see `alias`.
fieldSyntax.installSpec: the exact string handed to `dsh plugin --profile web add`. Reproduces the sync.sh pnpm_ins argument verbatim.
fieldSyntax.origin: `fetched` = resolved from a remote (git, tarball, npm) at install time. `vendored` = the source lives in this repository and is installed from a path.
fieldSyntax.source: where the bytes come from: type git|tarball|npm|in-repo, plus repo/url/path.
fieldSyntax.pin: kind + value + immutability. `immutability` is how hard it is for the bytes behind this pin to change without a change in this file: sha > short-sha > npm-version > tag > none.
fieldSyntax.alias: present only when packageName differs from the upstream package's own name. Never remove one without reading its `why`.
fieldSyntax.plane: host | client | both. Host-plane code runs in the DSH node process with the process's full authority; client-plane code runs in the browser page with full page authority. Neither is sandboxed.
fieldSyntax.why: MANDATORY. Why this is installed, in words a stranger can act on: what breaks or is missing without it.
fieldSyntax.allowBuilds: whether pnpm must be allowed to run this package's lifecycle scripts, and the exact pnpm-workspace.yaml key if so. See `allowBuildsPolicy`.
fieldSyntax.trust: tier from `trustTiers`, plus the basis for the assignment. Advisory today; a later ticket automates the evidence.
fieldSyntax.lastReviewed: the date someone last LOOKED AT THIS PIN and confirmed it is the pin we intend to install. It does NOT assert that the code at that pin was read -- `trust.tier` says that, and `trust.codeReviewed` says it plainly.
fieldSyntax.notes: carried-forward prose from sync.sh and the web patch: context that is true but not a rule.
fieldSyntax.hazards: carried-forward prose that IS a rule. Each one records a failure that already happened. Read before bumping, renaming, or removing.

$comment: Every entry in this roster runs in the SAME cordis composition as bash-guard,
mcp-servers and dsh-remote. Host-plane entries get the DSH process's full
authority -- filesystem, network, subprocess, session data, tool registration --
with no sandbox and no capability boundary between plugins. A client-plane entry
gets the whole page, including the session transcript and every credential the
page can reach. There is no tier that means 'safe'; the tiers rank only HOW MUCH
IS KNOWN about the code, and the honest answer for most of this roster is: the
pin is fixed and nobody here has read it.
trustTiers.first-party: Authored in this repository or by its author, and reviewed as ordinary source in ordinary review. The pin, if any, points at a commit written here.
trustTiers.maintained-fork: Third-party code forked by this repository's author and pinned to a commit authored here. The DELTA from upstream is known and was written deliberately; the BASE it forks is third-party code nobody here has audited. Do not read this tier as 'ours'.
trustTiers.pinned-unreviewed: Third-party code, pinned to a specific ref, never read by anyone here. It is trusted for exactly one reason: the pin cannot silently change under us. Bumping the pin is a new trust decision, not a routine update.
trustTiers.unpinned: Resolved at install time from a range or a moving ref, so the code can change with no change in this repository. A DEFECT TIER. No entry should sit here; one that does is a bug to fix, not a state to accept.

$comment: Carried from step_allow_builds(). pnpm 10+ refuses to run a package's
install/build lifecycle scripts unless its EXACT RESOLVED tarball URL is listed
under `allowBuilds` in the web profile's pnpm-workspace.yaml. The install engine
must reconstruct that URL the same way pnpm does, because the URL contains the
pin and therefore changes on every bump.
allowBuildsPolicy.derivation: From a `github:owner/repo#ref` spec: path = spec minus the `github:` prefix and minus `#ref`; ref = everything after the last `#`; name = basename(path). Emit `  <name>@<tarball>: true` under an `allowBuilds:` block, creating the block if absent. Idempotent: skip if the exact line is already present.
allowBuildsPolicy.onBump: The key embeds the ref, so bumping any pin whose entry has allowBuilds.required=true invalidates its old key. Re-derive; do not hand-edit. Stale keys are inert but should be pruned.

applyEntryPatches assigns each override key WHOLESALE (target[key] = value, in dsh-app-boot/lib/index.js). It does NOT deep-merge, so the config override block must repeat EVERY default from the plugin's own cordis.patch.yml. Only two values differ from those defaults: session.secure (true, because the proxy terminates TLS so the cookie may carry Secure) and debug (registers POST /auth/trace, which writes client trace lines to the server journal; keep it false unless debugging a remote-mode fault -- the client half only ships traces when the page URL also carries ?dshTrace=1).

source.upstream: dsh-compaction-instant, published 0.1.4; forked by this repository's author

pin.note: Full sha off the fork's compat/dsh-0.1.5 branch, taken from published 0.1.4. Upgrading = bumping this pin.

alias.why: Installing UNDER THE BASIC NAME shadows the builtin compaction package instead of adding a second one. The composition patch then names @deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic for all three rows (compaction-instant, tool-recall via .../tool, and the engine the /compact command uses).

entries.why: Deterministic instant compaction: it shrinks a long session on a fixed rule instead of asking a model to summarise, so compaction is predictable and cheap. Upstream's automatic compaction fails outright on some sessions (see hazards), which is why this is a fork and not the published package.

trust.basis: Forked, patched and pinned by this repository's author; the fork's own fixes were written and exercised here. The base is third-party. Host-plane, and it REWRITES SESSION HISTORY -- a bug here destroys context rather than leaking it, which is why the fork exists.

notes: Fork behaviour: triggers on SURFACE tokens alone, compactAtTokens 250000 down to compactToTokens 15000, held as a RATIO so a surface that overshot the trigger earns a proportionately larger checkpoint.
Fork behaviour: drops errored tool calls and todo_write bookkeeping from the checkpoint, and reports the token size of every dropped tool result so the agent can see what its own calls cost.

The skill-gate config alwaysDeny list hides this package's `search` and `recall` tools from every agent unconditionally: they are superseded by resume_search/resume_read from the resume plugin, and no skill may re-expose them.
hazards: INSTALL NAME: the package declares its own dsh.bundle patch, so a direct install under its REAL name inserts compaction rows the web patch already inserts and boot dies on a duplicate loader entry id. It must stay installed under @deepseek-ai/dsh-compaction-basic.
UPSTREAM BUG 1 (retention): a node larger than the retain ceiling crashes range selection, failing every automatic compaction on such a session.
UPSTREAM BUG 2 (checkpoint cap): the checkpoint cap ignores the span, so the compiler elides nothing.
UPSTREAM BUG 3 (framing cost): the fixed framing cost then makes the checkpoint LARGER than what it replaces.

UPSTREAM BUG 4 (self-consumption): compaction consumed its own checkpoints. Absorbing a prior checkpoint whole nested the envelopes and freed almost nothing; automatic pressure then read the token meter's ANCHORED REQUEST TOTAL, which also counts the system prompt, the tool schemas and cache read/write tokens, so an irreducible floor held the session above the threshold -- compaction re-fired at the next step and ate the checkpoint it had just written.
Do NOT track upstream main: it imports @deepseek-ai/dsh-util-values, which needs dsh 0.1.2.

The `command-compact` re-enable MUST be a top-level override row, NOT a child of the insert list: dsh-base already owns that id and a second one kills boot with 'duplicate loader entry id: command-compact'. dsh-base mounts command-compact on the host plane and dsh-web-app disables it (the web app moves the compaction backend to the preset plane); because this bundle keeps a compaction engine on the HOST plane, /compact belongs there too and must not depend on which preset a session uses.

pin.note: There is no remote ref: this repository's git history IS the pin. The version string records the dsh RC it forks. It must be re-checked on every dsh upgrade, because it shadows a builtin that upgrades with dsh.

alias.why: Same name as the builtin ON PURPOSE, so the vendored fork is what the profile resolves. The composition mounts it as the llm-pi-ai-affinity row and DISABLES the builtin llm-pi-ai row.

entries.why: Vendored fork of the dsh llm-pi-ai builtin that adds session-affinity headers on anthropic-messages routes, so a session's requests keep landing on the same upstream and the provider cache is actually hit. The stock builtin has no affinity and cannot be configured into having it.

trust.basis: Third-party base (a dsh builtin) vendored into this repository with a local delta. Vendoring means the bytes are visible in review and cannot change without a commit here -- the strongest position in the roster -- but the 0.1.5-rc.3 base itself has not been read. Host-plane: it is the LLM adapter, so it sees every prompt and every credential on the route.

notes: Unlike every other vendored plugin package its lib/ IS the source -- there is no src/ -- so nothing in it is build output (config/migration-map.json rule df-plugin-llm-pi-ai says the same).
This is the roster's worked example of a VENDORED entry; every other entry here is fetched.
hazards: The builtin llm-pi-ai composition row MUST stay disabled while this is installed. The vendored fork, linked into the web profile under the same package name, is the only pi-ai adapter registrar; leaving the builtin enabled registers the adapter twice.
Re-check on every dsh upgrade: it forks 0.1.5-rc.3, and a dsh bump can move the builtin out from under the fork.

2026-10-06 re-base: re-vendored from 0.1.0-rc.8 onto the 0.1.5-rc.3 builtin. The 're-check on every dsh upgrade' hazard fired exactly as documented: @deepseek-ai/dsh-llm 0.1.5-rc.3 renamed CallId to ToolCallId and offloadRequestImages to offloadRequestImagesWithPolicy (plus offloadedImagePrefixCount/offloadedImageText), which broke the old fork's import at boot. The 4-hunk affinity delta (anthropic-messages sendSessionAffinityHeaders withhold->offer, compatProfile sendSessionAffinityHeaders schema field, parseRetryAfterMs helper + export) was ported onto the new base; upstream also added supportsMidConvoEffort/allowedFallbackModels to the anthropic gate, chatTemplateArgs/thinking-budget fields to compatProfile, and dsh-util-values/dsh-brand imports, all carried through untouched.

$comment: Packages deliberately NOT installed, and the reason. These are the most
expensive comments in sync.sh to lose: each one records a mistake that was made
or narrowly avoided, and without them the obvious next move is to install the
thing again. An install engine should treat this list as a denylist and refuse
an entry whose packageName appears here.

$comment: The rest of step_install_plugins: this repository's OWN plugin packages,
installed from a path (`$HERE/plugins/<name>`) rather than fetched. They are
listed here so that nothing in step_install_plugins is lost when the shell
function is deleted, and so the derived extra-plugin check has the full set of
expected dependency names -- but they are NOT third-party roster entries: they
have no pin, no upstream and no trust question, and in Thursday they become
workspace packages under packages/plugins/ that the engine links, not installs.
Every one of them is tier `first-party`, origin `vendored`, allowBuilds false.

packages.why: Archive and restore sessions from the UI.
Provider subscription panel; needs the user's own credentials at runtime, but ships none.
The tool-card renderer: turns raw tool calls and results into readable cards.
Browser half of the profiles host plugin: the profile/route picker UI.
Lets the human attach a comment when approving or rejecting, so a rejection says why.

The todo panel that survives an interrupt. The official todos projection clears on every turn/start, so the panel blanks as soon as the next message goes out; this mirrors the list into a projection that ignores turn/start. The shipped context ring reads a provider figure that only ever GROWS. This replaces it with one measured from the surface, so the ring falls after a compaction instead of pinning at full.

dsh hardcodes its font tokens on :root and its monospace stack ends at a named font with NO `monospace` generic, so the browser never reaches the font the system is configured with. This overrides both tokens from html:root, which outranks :root without needing !important.
Styled tooltips. An element opts in with data-dsh-tip and KEEPS its own title attribute, which stays the fallback: if this package fails or never loads, the browser shows the native tooltip.

$comment: step_report_extra_plugins() keeps a hand-maintained `expected` array and warns
in three separate comments to keep it in sync with the pnpm_ins list. That

derivedChecks.expectedDependencies: the union of entries[].packageName and workspacePlugins.packages[].packageName
derivedChecks.profileBaseNote: The web profile's own base deps. They are installed by dsh, not by this roster, and must not be reported as extras.
derivedChecks.extraPluginPolicy: A dependency of the web profile that is in neither set is an EXTRA: the install engine prints it and prints the exact `dsh plugin --profile web remove <name>` command, and never removes it itself. Installing only ever adds, so a package dropped from this roster stays installed until a human removes it.
